candidate.name: DISJOINT_COPY_SELECTOR_OR_MERGE
candidate.definition: Rename the variables of A and B to disjoint copies A# and B#. Introduce a fresh selector s and output {s OR C : C in A#} union {not s OR D : D in B#}.
candidate.exact_sat_semantics: SAT(M)=SAT(A) OR SAT(B). Disjoint renaming is valid because SAT-OR does not require the two branches to share an assignment.

theorem.statement: If delta*(A)=a>=1 and delta*(B)=b>=1, then delta*(M)=a+b-1.
proof: Take any nonempty clause subset Q of M and split it into guarded A-part QA and guarded B-part QB.
If only QA is nonempty, every clause contains selector s, so deficiency(Q)=deficiency(QA_un_guarded)-1 <= a-1; symmetrically for B.
If both parts are nonempty, the renamed branch variable sets are disjoint and s is the only shared variable. Hence deficiency(Q)=deficiency(QA_un_guarded)+deficiency(QB_un_guarded)-1 <= a+b-1.
Because a,b>=1, there are nonempty sub-clause-sets A0,B0 attaining maximum deficiencies a,b. Taking both guarded copies gives deficiency exactly a+b-1.
Therefore maximum deficiency is exactly a+b-1.

R44BD_effect.children: If both normalized children have maximum deficiency exactly k-1>=1, the selector merge has maximum deficiency 2k-3.
R44BD_effect.rank_comparison: For k>=3, 2k-3 > k-1, so the merge fails R44BD obligation M2 delta*(M)<=k-1.
R44BD_effect.best_case_note: Renaming branch variables apart removes the additional overlap term present when the children share variables. Thus this barrier already holds in the selector construction's maxdef-friendliest disjoint-copy form.
R44BD_effect.k2_boundary: For k=2 and a=b=1 the formula gives delta*(M)=1, so this theorem does not block that special layer.

overlap_extension.identity: Without disjoint renaming, for a mixed subset QA,QB the deficiency equals delta(QA)+delta(QB)-1+|Var(QA) intersect Var(QB)|.
overlap_extension.meaning: Shared semantic variables can only increase the mixed-subset deficiency relative to the disjoint-copy baseline.
